idiom_name: case/when (=== matching) over the decoded message, or a frozen Hash of lambdas keyed by kind
implementation_notes: Ruby's case expression matches each when branch with ===, so a branch can be a literal, a Regexp, a Range, a class or a lambda (verified in the control-expressions reference), which lets the routing conditions be written directly as branch predicates with an else as the fallback; the first matching branch wins, so branch order is the rule precedence. The frozen Hash-of-procs form with fetch gives rules-as-data and constant-time lookup, and since 2.7 the in keyword adds structural pattern matching for hash and array payloads. Message frameworks route by queue or topic name (Sidekiq queue per job class, Karafka consumer per topic), so a decision that needs the body stays in this dispatcher.
pitfalls: Parsed JSON gives string keys while internal messages often use symbols: msg[:kind] versus msg['kind'] makes every lookup miss and route to the fallback without raising anything.
A case without else returns nil and execution continues, so an unmatched message disappears unless the fallback branch is written explicitly.
Branch order is precedence and nothing checks it: a broad early condition (a Regexp or Range matching everything) shadows the specific branches behind it.
